23-008079.title: Oil Limited Energy Auditor Technician, Commercial or Residential
23-008079.description: Oil limited energy auditor technicians perform combustion safety and efficiency testing on oil-fired heating or oil-fired water heating equipment. Oil limited energy auditor technicians may not make any adjustments to oil-fired heating or oil-fired water heating equipment.
23-008079.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

00-78.title: Enrolled Actuary
00-78.description: Enrolled Actuaries meet experience requirements and pass an examination. EAs are experts on the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). The EA designation is awarded by the Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries, located at the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury. Renewal every 3 years requires continuing actuarial education and other professional development activities. For detailed information, see http://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-utl/20cfr901.pdf or http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/actuaries/index.html.
00-78.agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury · Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries

23-020001.title: Engineer, Professional (All Disciplines)
23-020001.description: Anyone practicing or offering to practice professional engineering in Maine must be qualified and must be licensed with the State of Maine.
23-020001.agency: Maine Board of Registration of Professional Engineers

23-008186.title: Soil Scientist
23-008186.description: Soil scientists evaluate and interpret soils and soil-related data for the purpose of understanding soil resources as they contribute to agricultural production. Soil affects environmental quality and is managed for protection of human health and the environment.
23-008186.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

00-18.title: Air Traffic Control Tower Operator
00-18.description: Requirements to obtain an Air Traffic Control Tower Operator certificate include passing a written test. Besides the basic certificate, to act at any operating position, the individual must pass a practical test on control tower equipment and its use. To obtain a facility rating, the individual must have at least six months experience and pass another practical test. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked, although the individual must maintain current experience to work under the certificate. Detailed information can be found at web sites:http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, http://www.natca.org/assets/Documents/mediacenter/controller_brochure.pdf, http://www2.faa.gov/careers/employment/atc.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.31-65.50.

00-12.title: Aircraft Mechanic - A & P
00-12.description: Aircraft mechanics are certified by the FAA with either an airframe (A) or powerplant (P) rating. Initial ratings require either completion of FAA Approved Aviation Maintenance Technician School or 18 months of work experience. Applicants must pass written, oral and practical exams. Thirty months of work experience is required for a combined Airframe & Powerplant (A & P) certificate. To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an A & P certificate for at least 3 years. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, but requires currency of experience or refresher training. For further information, go the web site of the Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS): http://umet-vets.dol.gov/airframe-mechanic.htm, http://www1.faa.gov/AVR/afs/mechanics.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.71-65.95.

00-16.title: Aircraft Repairer
00-16.description: To be eligible for a repairman certificate, a person must have the qualifications needed on the job. These qualifications may be obtained through 18 months of work experience or completion of formal training. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www2.faa.gov/education/rlib/career.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.101-65.105.

00-02.title: Airline Transport Pilot
00-02.description: To become certified (licensed) as an Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), an individual must have a Commercial Pilot certificate or equivalent with an instrument rating for airplane, helicopter, or powered-lift (glider). Air flight training and ground school as well as flight experience are requirements. They also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. They must pass a written test and a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.151-61.167.

00-08.title: Commercial Pilot
00-08.description: All pilots who are paid to transport passengers or cargo must have a Commercial Pilot's license with an instrument rating issued by the FAA. To qualify for this license, the applicant must be at least 18 years old and have at least 250 hours of flight experience. The time can be reduced through participation in certain flight school curricula approved by the FAA. The individual also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. Passing a written test and a demonstration of flying ability are required. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.121-61.133 and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-15.title: Flight Engineer
00-15.description: To become certified as a Flight Engineer requires that the individual have either training or experience. Passing a written exam and a practical test and having a current medical certificate are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://umet-vets.dol.gov/flightengineer.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.31-63.43.

00-77.title: Flight Instructor
00-77.description: To obtain certification as a Flight Instructor, the individual must hold either a Commercial Pilot or Airline Transport Pilot certificate with appropriate aircraft and instrument ratings. Training is required as well as experience in the type of aircraft being rated. This license is valid for 2 years and may be renewed by one of several options, such as passing a practical test, documenting student success, or taking a refresher course. More details can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.181-61.199, www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ.

00-20.title: Flight Navigator
00-20.description: To become certified as a Flight Navigator, the individual must be at least 21 years old and have a medical certificate. He or she must have both training in flight navigation and practical experience. Passing written and practical tests are required as well as having a current medical certificate. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended, or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.51-63.61.

00-13.title: Ground Instructor
00-13.description: To obtain certification as a Ground Instructor, the individual must pass an aircraft navigation knowledge test and a test of the fundamentals of instructing, unless the person already is employed as a teacher or holds a teacher's certification. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.211-61.217.

00-06.title: Private Pilot
00-06.description: Obtaining a Private Pilot certificate (license) requires the individual to complete ground and flight training, have flight experience, obtain a medical certificate, and pass a written exam as well as a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. The FAA Advisory Circular, AC 61-12M, Student Pilot Guide, outlines general procedures for obtaining student and private pilot certificates. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.102-61.117, and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

23-004002.title: Emergency Medical Dispatcher

00-60.title: Medical Doctor
00-60.description: A ship's Medical Doctor is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A medical doctor must also hold a valid license as a physician or surgeon issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

00-48.title: Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-48.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must, while holding a license as a Third Assistant Engineer, complete one of the following: 360 days of service as an Assistant Engineer; or a minimum of 180 days as an Assistant Engineer and 360 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 360 days as Chief Engineer (Limited-Oceans). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-48.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-38.title: Second Mate - Upper Level
00-38.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Mate Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on ocean steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Third Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

00-58.title: Radio Officer

Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-41.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-42.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

23-008195.description: Tramway inspectors perform inspections required on tramways in the State of Maine.

23-cdl.title: Commercial Drivers License (CDL)
23-cdl.description: Commercial Drivers Licenses are issued by state departments but are similar from state to state, since the minimum requirements of the licenses and endorsements are set centrally. For more information contact the state DMV or https://cms.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/commercial-drivers-license/how-do-i-get-commercial-drivers-license.

23-108312.description: Radiographers assist radiologists and other physicians and use diagnostic equipment to identify illnesses and injuries. A trainee learns under a radiographer.

23-008210.description: Chiropractic acupuncturists use both chiropractic care and acupuncture to treat their clients.

23-008305.title: Chiropractic Acupuncturist
23-008305.description: Chiropractor Acupuncture means the insertion of acupuncture needles through the skin at strategic points. It is a chiropractic methodology used for the correction of the soft tissue components contributing to subluxation and the accompanying physiological or mechanical abnormalities. Except as provided in section 502, chiropractic acupuncture may only be practiced by a licensee who has received a chiropractic acupuncture certification from the board.

23-008048.title: Chiropractor
23-008048.description: Chiropractors are healthcare professionals who use techniques to alleviate problems in their patients' neuromusculoskeletal systems. They perform spinal adjustments, massage clients, and use ultrasounds to reduce the pain or tension that their patients experience.
23-008048.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008066.description: Any credit reporting agency (credit bureau) used by creditors in Maine must be registered. 23-001043.title: Athletic Director
23-001043.description: Athletic directors generally oversee all aspects of an athletic program, including hiring coaches, scheduling, budget preparation, promotion, compliance, and facility management.
23-001043.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-001045.title: Cooperative Education Coordinator (9-12)
23-001045.description: Cooperative education coordinators manage the cooperative education program for all eligible students in grades 9 through 12, giving qualifying students the opportunity to participate in paid and unpaid apprenticeships or employment programs in their career interests for academic credit.
23-001045.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-001013.title: Principal, Teaching
23-001013.description: Principals lead teachers and staff, set goals and ensure students meet their learning objectives. Overseeing a school's day-to-day operations may inlcude handling disciplinary matters, managing a budget and hiring teachers and other personnel.
23-001013.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-001044.title: School Nurse (K-12)
23-001044.description: School nurses are specialist nursing professionals that are responsible for caring to students with illnesses and injuries and advancing the health of students and staff within the school environment.
23-001044.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-001024.title: Teacher (various primary, secondary and adult)
23-001024.description: Teachers are responsible for preparing lesson plans and educating students at all levels. Their duties include assigning homework, grading tests, and documenting progress.
23-001024.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-019015.title: Dental Assistant, Expanded Function (EFDA)
23-019015.description: Expanded function dental assistant means an individual licensed by this board who performs duties under the direct and general supervision of a dentist.

23-019016.title: Dental Faculty (Dentist, Dental Hygienist, Denturist)
23-019016.description: A faculty license means a license issued to an individual who teaches dentistry, dental hygiene or denturism as part of a clinical and didactic program and is authorized to practice only within the school setting.

23-019011.title: Dental Hygiene Therapist, Authority and Authority Provisional
23-019011.description: Dental hygiene therapy authority means a dental hygienist licensed by this board who is authorized to practice dental hygiene therapy. A written practice agreement with a licensed dentist is required pursuant to the Dental Practice Act and practice standards identified by board rules.

23-019001.title: Dental Hygienist (and Temporary)
23-019001.description: Dental hygienist means an individual licensed by this board who engages in the practice of dental hygiene. A dental hygienist practices under the general and direct supervision of a dentist.

23-019013.title: Dental Hygienist Local Anesthesia, Authority
23-019013.description: Local anesthesia authority is granted to a dental hygienist to administer local anesthesia under the direct supervision of a dentist.

23-019012.title: Dental Hygienist Nitrous Oxide Analgesia, Authority
23-019012.description: Nitrous oxide analgesia authority is granted to a qualified dental hygienist to administer nitrous oxide analgesia under the direct supervision of a dentist.

23-019010.title: Dental Hygienist, Independent Practice
23-019010.description: Independent practice dental hygienist means an individual licensed by this board who is authorized to practice independent dental hygiene. A written practice agreement with a licensed dentist to interpret dental radiographs is required pursuant to the Dental Practice Act and practice standards identified by board rules.

23-019009.title: Dental Hygienist, Public Health
23-019009.description: Public health dental hygiene means a dental hygienist licensed by this board is authorized to practice public health dental hygiene. A written practice agreement with a licensed dentist is required pursuant to the Dental Practice Act and practice standards identified by board rules.

23-019002.title: Dental Radiographer
23-019002.description: Dental radiographer means an individual licensed by this board to practice dental radiography under the supervision of a dentist or a dental hygienist practicing with an independent practice dental hygiene authority.

23-019006.title: Dental Sedation, Deep/General Anesthesia
23-019006.description: A permit issued to a dentist to administer all levels of sedation and general anesthesia in accordance with Chapter 14 of the board's rules.

23-019005.title: Dental Sedation, Moderate I & II
23-019005.description: A permit issued to a dentist to administer moderate sedation at the level permitted in accordance with Chapter 14 of the board's rules.

23-019003.title: Dentist (and Temporary)
23-019003.description: Dentist means an individual licensed by this board who engages in the practice of dentistry. A dentist may also have supervisory responsibilities of individuals who are also licensed by the board such as dental hygienists, dental hygiene therapists, public health dental hygienists, dental radiographers, and expanded function dental assistants.

23-019007.title: Dentist, Limited (Retired)
23-019007.description: Limited dentist means an individual licensed to practice dentistry solely in a nonprofit dental clinic without any remuneration for work performed at the clinic.

23-019008.title: Dentist, Resident
23-019008.description: Resident dentist permit means a permit issued to an individual who has graduated from a dental educational program to practice dentistry for the purpose of gaining clinical skills under the supervision of a dentist in board approved settings.

23-008068.title: Dietitian
23-008068.description: Dietitians assess patients' and clients' nutritional and health needs. They counsel patients on nutrition issues and healthy eating habits and develop meal and nutrition plans, taking both clients' preferences and budgets into account. Dietitians are typically in charge of dietetic techs.
23-008068.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008070.title: Dietitian, Temporary
23-008070.description: Dietitians assess patients' and clients' nutritional and health needs. They counsel patients on nutrition issues and healthy eating habits and develop meal and nutrition plans, taking both clients' preferences and budgets into account. Dietitians are typically in charge of dietetic techs. A temporary license is awarded before completion of the exam.
23-008070.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008071.title: Electrician, Apprentice
23-008071.description: Electrician apprentices support electricians in the maintenance, operation and repair of electrical systems.
23-008071.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008073.title: Electrician, Helper
23-008073.description: Electrician helpers support electricians in the maintenance, operation and repair of electrical systems.
23-008073.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008074.title: Electrician, Journeyman-in-Training
23-008074.description: A journeyman-in-training electrician is a person making electrical installations in the employment of a master electrician, limited electrician or electrical company and under the supervision of a journeyman, limited or master electrician.
23-008074.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008075.title: Electrician, Limited
23-008075.description: Limited electricians install and service the electrical work related to a specific type of electrically operated equipment or to specific electrical installations only authorized by this license. Limited licenses are issued for the following categories: Low Energy, Gas Dispense, House Wiring, Outdoor Signs, Refrigeration, Traffic Signals, Water Pumps, and Crane Technicians.
23-008075.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008076.title: Electrician, Master
23-008076.description: Master electricians install electrical wires, conduits, apparatus, fixtures and other electrical equipment.
23-008076.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-108305.title: Helper Electrician, Senior Helper Electrician
23-108305.description: Electrician helpers support electricians in the maintenance, operation and repair of electrical systems.
23-108305.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-108307.title: Journeyman Electrician, Senior Journeyman Electrician
23-108307.description: Journey electricians are able to provide electrical repairs and services and are usually on their way to getting a master electrician license.
23-108307.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-108306.title: Limited Electrician, Senior Limited Electrician
23-108306.description: A limited electrician is an individual licensed to make electrical installations limited to a specific type of electrically operated equipment or to specific electrical installations only authorized by this license.
23-108306.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008308.title: Elevator Contractor
23-008308.description: Any person, firm, partnership, association, corporation or company engaged in the installation, sale, service, maintenance or inspection of elevators in this state shall register with the board annually. The registration must include the names and addresses of all licensed private inspectors, licensed mechanics and all helpers employed by the elevator contractor.
23-008308.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008077.title: Elevator Inspector
23-008077.description: Elevator inspectors inspect elevators and lifts to make sure they comply to safety standards.
23-008077.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008078.title: Elevator Mechanic
23-008078.description: Elevator mechanics service, repair, alter or install elevators and lifts.
23-008078.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008084.title: Funeral Practitioner
23-008084.description: Funeral service practitioners meet with families, help families plan services, embalm and prepare bodies, plan and organize wakes and memorial services, place obituary notices in newspapers and handle paperwork.
23-008084.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-004001.title: Emergency Medical Services Provider
23-004001.description: EMS providers respond to emergency calls to provide efficient and immediate care to the critically ill and injured, and to transport the patient to a medical facility. There are four levels of “EMT” license recognized by Maine EMS: Emergency Medical Responder (EMR), Emergency Medical Technician (EMT), Advanced EMT, and Paramedic. These levels are defined by the education and skills requirements as well as the scope of practice.
23-004001.agency: Maine Department of Public Safety · Office of Emergency Medical Services

23-004003.title: Emergency Medical Technician-Paramedic
23-004003.description: EMS providers respond to emergency calls to provide efficient and immediate care to the critically ill and injured, and to transport these patients to a medical facility. There are four levels of “EMT” licenses recognized by Maine EMS: Emergency Medical Response.
23-004003.agency: Maine Department of Public Safety · Office of Emergency Medical Services

23-008323.title: Propane and Natural Gas Helper
23-008323.description: A propane and natural gas helper is a person licensed by the board to assist a licensed technician. A helper must work under the direct and continuous supervision of a licensed technician on-site.
23-008323.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008006.title: Aesthetician
23-008006.description: Aestheticians clean and maintain a client's skin by performing facials, waxing, chemical peels, skin treatments and body treatments.
23-008006.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008306.title: Aesthetician Instructor
23-008306.description: An aesthetician instructor means a person who may instruct in any of the branches of aesthetics, barbering, limited barbering, cosmetology or nail technology contingent on the possession of a valid license to practice and is authorized to instruct in each respective practice issued under this chapter. Physicians may instruct without holding a license to practice in a branch of aesthetics, barbering, limited barbering, cosmetology or nail technology.
23-008306.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008007.title: Aesthetician, Apprentice
23-008007.description: Aesthetician apprentices learn to clean and maintain a client's skin by performing facials, waxing, chemical peels, skin treatments and body treatments.
23-008007.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008009.title: Aesthetician, Temporary Permit
23-008009.description: Aestheticians clean and maintain a client's skin by performing facials, waxing, chemical peels, skin treatments and body treatments. Temporary licenses are awarded to those who have completed the education requirements or can prove they are licensed in another state.

23-008105.title: Investment Advisor

00-FinOpL.title: Series 39 - Direct Participation Programs Limited Principal

23-011001.title: Body Piercer

23-012001.title: Certified Nursing Assistants
23-012001.description: Certified nursing assistants assist RNs in their duties. To be placed on the Maine CNA Registry, you must be able to provide official documentation of formal CNA training that meets Maine’s Rules and Regulations as well as Federal OBRA Regulations, whether for immediate placement on the Registry or for completing the “Non-Traditional CNA Competency Testing Evaluation testing.
23-012001.agency: Maine Department of Health and Human Services · Division of Licensing and Certification

23-011002.title: Combined Body Piercing & Tattoo
23-011002.description: See pages for "Tattoo Artist" and "Body Piercing" licenses.
23-011002.agency: Maine Department of Health and Human Services · Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention

23-011003.title: Micropigmentation
23-011003.description: Micropigmentation is the process of placing very small granules of pigment under the skin.
23-011003.agency: Maine Department of Health and Human Services · Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention

23-003004.title: Polygraph Examiner
23-003004.description: Polygraph examiners use a variety of instruments to measure respiratory, sweat gland, and cardiovascular responses to questions posed during oral examinations. They then interpret the results of the examinations to render an opinion as to the truthfulness of the examinee's responses.
23-003004.agency: Maine Department of Public Safety · Maine State Police

23-008300.title: Forester, Intern
23-008300.description: Intern forester means a person authorized by the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation under the sponsorship of a licensed forester to perform professional services requiring the application of forestry principles and techniques, including investigations, consultations, development of forest management plans, supervision of forest management, forest utilization, forest economics or other forestry activities carried out in connection with public or private lands.
23-008300.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008080.title: Forester, Registered Professional
23-008080.description: Foresters offer professional services requiring the application of forestry principles and techniques, including investigations, consultations, development of forest management plans, supervision of forest management, forest utilization, forest economics or other forestry activities carried out in connection with public or private lands.
23-008080.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008301.title: Forester, Supervisor or Unlicensed
23-008301.description: A Forester may register with the board to supervise and direct an unlicensed person in the practice of forestry.
23-008301.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008046.title: Charitable Organization (Professional Solicitor)
23-008046.description: Professional solicitors solicit contributions from the public on behalf of a charitable organization in exchange for a fee or other remuneration.
23-008046.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008082.title: Funeral "Home" Establishment
23-008082.description: A funeral home, funeral parlor, or mortuary is a business that provides interment and funeral services for the dead and their families.
23-008082.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008083.title: Funeral Director and Practitioner (Inactive)
23-008083.description: Funeral directors meet with families, help families plan services, embalm and prepare bodies, plan and organize wakes and memorial services, place obituary notices in newspapers and handle paperwork.
23-008083.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008085.title: Funeral Practitioner Trainee
23-008085.description: Funeral service practitioner trainees learn to meet with families, help families plan services, embalm and prepare bodies, plan and organize wakes and memorial services, place obituary notices in newspapers and handle paperwork.
23-008085.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008086.title: Geologist
23-008086.description: Geologists study the composition, structure, and other physical attributes of the earth, including rocks and minerals. They use physics, mathematics, and geological knowledge in exploration for oil, gas, minerals, or underground water.
23-008086.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-023004.title: Nurse Midwife (Advanced Practice RN)
23-023004.description: "Advanced practice registered nurse" means an individual who is currently licensed under this chapter to practice advanced practice registered nursing as defined in subsection 2-A.

23-008314.title: Multi-Level Long Term Care Facility Administrator
23-008314.description: A "Multi-Level Long Term Care Facility Administrator" is a licensed individual who has responsibility for the general administration of a Multi-Level Long Term Care Facility, a Nursing Home, or a Residential Care Facility. A "Multi-Level Long Term Care Facility" is a medical care facility, other than a hospital, that provides more than one level of long term care, including care levels normally associated with nursing homes and those associated with residential care / assisted living.
23-008314.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008133.title: Nursing Home Administrator
23-008133.description: Nursing home administrators supervise, plan, develop, monitor and maintain appropriate standards of care throughout all departments in the nursing home.
23-008133.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008316.title: Nursing Home Administrator-In-Training
23-008316.description: "Administrator-in-Training" means an individual who meets the qualifications set forth in rules by the board, is engaged in a training program defined in rules and approved by the board and is under the supervision of a preceptor also approved by the board.
23-008316.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008134.title: Nursing Home Administrator, Temporary
23-008134.description: Nursing home administrators supervise, plan, develop, monitor and maintain appropriate standards of care throughout all departments in the nursing home. Temporary licenses are valid for 90 days.
23-008134.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008315.title: Residential Care Facility Administrator
23-008315.description: "Residential Care Facility Administrator" is an individual who has responsibility for the general administration of a residential care facility. A residential care facility refers to a Level II Residential Care Facility having a licensed capacity for seven or more residents, and whose services provided fall within the definition of a medical care facility other than a hospital.
23-008315.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008179.title: Social Worker, Licensed
23-008179.description: Social workers help individuals, families and communities handle everyday life problems. They often assist clients who have issues caused by neglect, abuse, domestic violence, mental health and parental substance abuse.
23-008179.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008183.title: Social Worker, Licensed Clinical
23-008183.description: Clinical social workers will observe client behavior, assess needs and create treatment strategies. They also diagnose psychological, behavioral and emotional disorders.
23-008183.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008181.title: Social Worker, Licensed Master
23-008181.description: Social workers help individuals, families and communities handle everyday life problems. They often assist clients who have issues caused by neglect, abuse, domestic violence, mental health and parental substance abuse.
23-008181.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008182.title: Social Worker, Licensed Master-Conditional Clinical
23-008182.description: Clinical social workers will observe client behavior, assess needs and create treatment strategies. They also diagnose psychological, behavioral and emotional disorders.
23-008182.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008180.title: Social Worker, Licensed-Conditional
23-008180.description: Social workers help individuals, families and communities handle everyday life problems. They often assist clients who have issues caused by neglect, abuse, domestic violence, mental health and parental substance abuse. An exam is not required for a conditional license.
23-008180.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008087.title: Hearing Aid Dealer & Fitter
23-008087.description: Hearing aid dealer and fitters select and fit hearing aids for customers.
23-008087.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008089.title: Hearing Aid Dealer/Fitter Trainee (Temporary)
23-008089.description: Hearing aid dealer and fitter trainees learn to select and fit hearing aids for customers.
23-008089.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008212.title: Speech-Language Pathology Assistant
23-008212.description: Speech-language pathologist assistants meet minimum qualifications that the board may establish for Speech-Language Pathology Assistants, which are less than those qualifications established for licensure, but which must include an Associate's Degree or its equivalent as determined by the board, in the field of Communication Disorders.
23-008212.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008307.title: Lift Mechanic
23-008307.description: A lift mechanic is a person who services, repairs, alters or installs lifts in the State of Maine.
23-008307.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008127.title: Manufactured Housing Mechanic
23-008127.description: Manufactured housing mechanics install, repair, and replace units, fixtures, appliances, and other items and systems in mobile and modular homes, prefabricated buildings, or travel trailers using hand tools or power tools.
23-008127.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-003001.title: Motor Vehicle Inspection Mechanic, Certified
23-003001.description: Inspection mechanics inspect and assess the condition of all of the vehicle's essential mechanical systems and components.
23-003001.agency: Maine Department of Public Safety · Maine State Police

23-008137.title: Oil Burner Technician, Apprentice
23-008137.description: Apprentice oil burner technicians learn to install and repair systems that heat and power homes and businesses.
23-008137.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008138.title: Oil Burner Technician, Journeyman
23-008138.description: Journeyman oil burner technicians work with masters to learn to install and repair systems that heat and power homes and businesses.
23-008138.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008139.title: Oil Burner Technician, Master
23-008139.description: Master oil burner technicians install and repair systems that heat and power homes and businesses.
23-008139.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-001003.title: Curriculum Coordinator/Instructional Supervisor
23-001003.description: Curriculum coordinators are responsible for assisting in the development, revision, implementation, and evaluation of school curriculum. The coordinator is also responsible for developing and providing opportunities for teacher training and in-service activities related to the school's curriculum and initiatives.
23-001003.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

00-Ins.title: NIPR Insurance Registry
00-Ins.description: Licensed Insurance Occupations must also be registered at the federal level.

23-008303.title: Interior Designer, Certified
23-008303.description: Certified interior designers are certified to use the title "certified interior designer" after having met the requirements for certification, and design the interior of structures in order to achieve a visually pleasing look.
23-008303.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008304.title: Interpreters and Translators
23-008304.description: Contact the licensing agency for details.
23-008304.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008160.title: Psychologist (including Conditional and Temporary)
23-008160.description: Psychologists often gather information and evaluate behavior through controlled laboratory experiments, psychoanalysis, or psychotherapy. They also may administer personality, performance, aptitude, or intelligence tests.
23-008160.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008161.title: Psychologist Examiner (including Conditional and Temporary)
23-008161.description: Psychological examiners may provide intervention, such as consultation, behavior management or social skills training under the supervision of a licensed psychologist.
23-008161.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-007008.title: Arborist, Apprentice, Landscape
23-007008.description: Apprentice arborists are unlicensed individuals working under the supervision of a licensed arborist. Apprentices cannot preform arboriculture work independently, as they must be under the supervision of a licensed arborist.
23-007008.agency: Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry · Division of Plant and Animal Health

23-007007.title: Arborist, First Class, Landscape
23-007007.description: First class landscape arborists are primarily concerned with the care of ornamental trees. They may occasionally work around utility lines, but the majority of their work is performed away from utility lines.
23-007007.agency: Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry · Division of Plant and Animal Health

23-007009.title: Arborist, Master Landscape
23-007009.description: Master landscape arborists have completed five years of experience as a first class arborist, have successfully completed the Master Arborist examination, and hold a valid Maine Pesticide Applicator License in category 3A – Outdoor Ornamentals or category 6A - Right of Way Vegetation Management.
23-007009.agency: Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry · Division of Plant and Animal Health

23-008120.title: Landscape Architect
23-008120.description: Landscape architects design attractive and functional public parks, gardens, playgrounds, residential areas, college campuses, and public spaces. They also plan the locations of buildings, roads, walkways, flowers, shrubs, and trees within these environments.
23-008120.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-010001.title: Attorney
23-010001.description: An attorney is a person who is legally qualified and licensed to represent a person in a legal matter, such as a transaction or lawsuit.

23-001009.title: Library Media Specialist
23-001009.description: A library media specialist is a trained professional who works in schools to help students and staff members find materials and learn to do research.
23-001009.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-007014.title: Beekeeper
23-007014.description: Beekeepers ensure that their hives remain healthy and productive, and for commercial production, profitable. Some keep bees for pollination programs in areas where wild bees and other pollinators are in short supply.
23-007014.agency: Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry · Division of Plant and Animal Health

23-005002.title: Commodity Dealer, Agricultural Products
23-005002.description: Sellers of various food and agricultural products. Licenses vary by product type.
23-005002.agency: Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry · Bureau of Agriculture · Quality Assurance and Regulations

23-023001.title: Nurse, Licensed Practical
23-023001.description: The practice of "practical nursing" means performing tasks and responsibilities for compensation within a structured health care setting, reinforcing the patient and family teaching program through health teaching, health counseling and provision of supportive and restorative care under the direction of a registered nurse or licensed or otherwise legally authorized physician, podiatrist or dentist.

23-008122.title: Nail Technician
23-008122.description: Nail technicians provide individualized nail services and treatments to clients, including manicures and pedicures.
23-008122.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008209.title: Nail Technician, Instructor
23-008209.description: Nail technician instructors teach others how to provide individualized nail services and treatments to clients, including manicures and pedicures.
23-008209.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008125.title: Nail Technician, Temporary Permit
23-008125.description: Nail technicians provide individualized nail services and treatments to clients, including manicures and pedicures. Temporary licenses are awarded to those who have completed the education requirements or can prove they are licensed in another state.

23-008125.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008123.title: Nail Technician, Trainee
23-008123.description: Nail technician trainees learn to provide individualized nail services and treatments to clients, including manicures and pedicures.
23-008123.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008042.title: Boxing Promoter
23-008042.description: Contact the licensing agency for details.
23-008042.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008059.title: Counselor, Marriage & Family
23-008059.description: Marriage and family counselors provide counseling to couples and families and assess and treat intrapersonal and interpersonal problems and other dysfunctional behaviors to assist in the overall development and adjustment of their clients.
23-008059.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008060.title: Counselor, Marriage & Family (Conditional)
23-008060.description: Marriage and family counselors provide counseling to assess and treat intrapersonal and interpersonal problems and other dysfunctional behaviors and assist in the overall development and adjustment of those served. This temporary conditional license can be awarded to someone who has met all license requirements except completion of the exam. The applicant must complete and pass the exam within 6 months.
23-008060.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008061.title: Counselor, Pastoral
23-008061.description: Pastoral counselors are trained mental health professionals that provide both psychological therapy and spiritual guidance to individuals, couples, families, and groups in various settings. Due to the nature of their counseling work, pastoral counselors must be highly trained in both psychology and theology.
23-008061.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008062.title: Counselor, Pastoral (Conditional)
23-008062.description: Pastoral counselors are trained mental health professionals that provide both psychological therapy and spiritual guidance to individuals, couples, families, and groups in various settings. Due to the nature of their counseling work, pastoral counselors must be highly trained in both psychology and theology. Conditional licenses are awarded to applicants so they can fulfill the supervised experience requirements. After they have achieved 3000 hours of supervised experience they may apply for regular licenses and practice independently.
23-008062.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008063.title: Counselor, Professional
23-008063.description: Professional counselors work as mental health service providers, whose main role is to assess people for disorders and provide courses of treatment. They also help children, teenagers, adults and the elderly deal with cognitive-behavioral, interpersonal and mental health issues.
23-008063.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008064.title: Counselor, Professional (Conditional)
23-008064.description: Professional counselors work as mental health service providers, whose main role is to assess people for disorders and provide courses of treatment. They also help children, teenagers, adults and the elderly deal with cognitive-behavioral, interpersonal and mental health issues. Conditional licenses are awarded to applicants so they can fulfill the supervised experience requirements. After they have achieved 2,000 hours of supervised experience, they may apply for regular licenses and practice independently.
23-008064.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008065.title: Counselor, Registered
23-008065.description: Only available to counselors who registered prior to August 1st, 2008. Registration does not imply or certify in any way that the registered counselors have met any standards or criteria of education or training. A registered counselor may not diagnose or treat mental health disorders.
23-008065.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008131.title: Massage Therapist
23-008131.description: Massage therapists treat clients by using their hands to manipulate muscles and other soft tissues of the body.
23-008131.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

23-001012.title: Building Administrator, Assistant
23-001012.description: Assistant building administrators are responsible for helping keep the building and grounds in good working order as to maintain a safe, clean, and healthy environment for students and staff.
23-001012.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-008047.title: Chiropractic Assistant
23-008047.description: Chiropractic assistants help chiropractors use techniques to alleviate problems in their patients' neuromusculoskeletal systems.
23-008047.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-001023.title: Superintendent, Assistant
23-001023.description: Assistant superintendents aid the superintendent in the daily operation of the district as well as the planning, implementing, directing and maintaining of district programs by providing a wide variety of complex and confidential administrative and secretarial support.
23-001023.agency: Maine Department of Education · Division of Certification and Credentialing

23-008176.title: Respiratory Care Associate
23-008176.description: Respiratory care associates provide therapy, management, rehabilitation, diagnostic evaluation and care, administered on the order of a physician or surgeon, to patients with deficiencies and abnormalities affecting the cardiopulmonary system and associated aspects of other bodily systems. An associates license can be earned if one has NBRC credentials or is licensed in another state.
23-008176.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008173.title: Respiratory Care Technician
23-008173.description: Respiratory care technicians provide therapy, management, rehabilitation, diagnostic evaluation and care, administered on the order of a physician or surgeon, to patients with deficiencies and abnormalities affecting the cardiopulmonary system and associated aspects of other bodily systems.
23-008173.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008175.title: Respiratory Care Technician, Temporary
23-008175.description: Respiratory care technicians provide therapy, management, rehabilitation, diagnostic evaluation and care, administered on the order of a physician or surgeon, to patients with deficiencies and abnormalities affecting the cardiopulmonary system and associated aspects of other bodily systems. A temporary license can be earned without taking an exam.
23-008175.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008174.title: Respiratory Care Therapist
23-008174.description: Respiratory care therapists provide therapy, management, rehabilitation, diagnostic evaluation and care, administered on the order of a physician or surgeon, to patients with deficiencies and abnormalities affecting the cardiopulmonary system and associated aspects of other bodily systems.
23-008174.agency: Maine Department of Professional & Financial Regulation · Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation

23-008328.title: Respiratory Care, Trainee
23-008328.description: Respiratory care practitioner means a person licensed as a respiratory therapist or as a respiratory care technician under this chapter. Respiratory care means the therapy, management, rehabilitation, diagnostic evaluation and care, administered on the order of a physician or surgeon, of patients with deficiencies and abnormalities affecting the cardiopulmonary system and associated aspects of other bodily system.
